# PolkaMeter

> PolkaMeter is a load-testing tool for Polkadot SDK (Substrate) chains, modeled on JMeter. An XML plan lists the steps; plugins prepare chain-specific transactions; the `polkameter` CLI submits them at controlled rates, checks every transaction against the finalized chain and writes a verdict (PASS, WARN, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE) with JMeter-compatible results. The substrate plugin, shipped with the CLI from v0.3.0, loads any chain with the standard System and Balances pallets without custom code.

Install from v0.3.0 with the install script, `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agustinustheo/polkameter/main/install.sh | sh`, which installs the CLI and the substrate plugin. <!-- v0.3.0: remove after release -->Until v0.3.0 is released, build both from the repository: `cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/agustinustheo/polkameter --branch main polkameter polkameter-substrate-plugin`. `cargo install --locked polkameter` installs only the CLI, never the plugin. Then register the plugin with `polkameter plugin install "$(command -v polkameter-substrate-plugin)"`. `polkameter init --rpc ws://127.0.0.1:9944` writes a starter plan for a chain. Secrets never go in plans: a plan names a credential profile, and `polkameter plugin credential PROFILE ENV_VAR` maps it to an environment variable.

## Start here

- [Getting started](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/getting-started.html): install the CLI, build and install the example plugin, run a plan, read the run directory
- [Stress-test a local dev chain](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/dev-chain.html): start a pinned dev chain, run the substrate plugin's example plans, and the same in GitHub Actions and GitLab CI
- [Use PolkaMeter with an AI assistant](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/ai-assistants.html): the Agent Skill, the Claude Code plugin marketplace and this file

## How-to guides

- [Install](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/install.html): install script, cargo, binstall, container, source
- [Run a load test](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/load-test.html): load plan skeleton, rate steps and ramps, validate, preflight and run
- [Read the results](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/reading-results.html): verdict, failure onset, max sustained rate, loss check
- [Run PolkaMeter in CI](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/ci.html): the GitHub Action, other CI systems, GitLab
- [Troubleshooting](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/troubleshooting.html): common errors and fixes

## Reference

- [The substrate plugin](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/substrate-plugin.html): operations preflight, fund-accounts, prepare-remarks, prepare-transfers, check-state; their inputs and outputs; `polkameter init`
- [Plan](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/plans.html): every plan element and attribute, references, validation rules
- [CLI](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/cli.html): commands, flags, exit codes, environment variables
- [Run directory](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/results.html): every file a run writes
- [Plugins and SDK](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/plugins.html): plugin protocol, manifest, PreparedTx, state checks, the polkameter-plugin-sdk crate
- [Release assets](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/release-assets.html): archive names and contents

## Writing a plugin

- [Writing a plugin](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/writing-a-plugin.html): a plugin crate from scratch, for runtimes the substrate plugin cannot load
- [How a run works](https://agustinustheodorus.com/polkameter/how-it-works.html): phases of a run, from preflight to the report

## Optional

- [Source repository](https://github.com/agustinustheo/polkameter): CLI, SDK, substrate plugin, example plans in `examples/`
- [Agent Skill](https://github.com/agustinustheo/polkameter/tree/main/skills/polkameter): SKILL.md, plan templates, CI templates and a setup checklist
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/agustinustheo/polkameter/blob/main/AGENTS.md): build and test commands for contributors
